transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm here because I've been experiencing really exhausting, extreme mood swings. For about seven months, I felt abnormally energetic, hyperactive, and on top of the world, but for the past three months, I've crashed into a deep depression where I feel completely empty, sad, and unmotivated. It has just been a really severe and overwhelming shift for me.
During these high or low periods, or even when your mood felt relatively normal, did you ever hear voices, see things others couldn't, or hold beliefs that others found highly unusual?

No, I have never experienced anything like that. I've never heard voices or seen things that weren't there, and I haven't had any unusual beliefs. It has really just been my extreme moods and energy levels that have been fluctuating so wildly.
During those seven months when you felt highly energetic and on top of the world, did this state cause major disruptions in your work or relationships, or did it ever lead to you being hospitalized?
To be honest, I'm not really sure how to answer that. I don't quite know if it caused major disruptions in my life or if I was hospitalized back then.
During that highly energetic period, did your family or friends express deep concern about your behavior, or did you do things that were unusually risky or reckless?
I don't really recall my family or friends expressing any deep concern about my behavior back then. I also don't think I did anything that was particularly risky or reckless during that time.
During those seven months of high energy, did you feel like your ability to work or get things done actually improved, or did it make it harder for you to focus and finish tasks?

I actually felt extremely active and started a lot of different projects at once, but it was really hard to finish any of them. My thoughts were spinning so fast and felt so disorganized that I just couldn't focus enough to get things done.
Have you ever been hospitalized or required emergency psychiatric care at any point in your life, whether for a high mood or a low mood?
No, I have never been hospitalized or needed emergency psychiatric care for my mood issues. I've always managed to get by without needing that level of urgent medical intervention.
During those seven months of high energy, did you find that you needed much less sleep than usual, perhaps feeling fully rested after only three or four hours?
I don't really recall having that specific experience with my sleep back then. I'm not entirely sure what my sleep patterns were like during those high-energy months.
During those seven months when you struggled to focus and finish projects, did this lead to severe consequences like losing a job, failing school, or the end of a relationship?

No, it didn't lead to extreme consequences like losing my job or ending any relationships. It was definitely highly disruptive and made daily life very difficult, but I managed to avoid those kinds of severe outcomes.
During those seven months of high energy, did other people notice a clear and obvious change in your behavior and mood compared to how you normally are?

I'm not entirely sure what others noticed, as I haven't thought much about their perspective. However, looking back, my behavior was definitely very different from my usual self during those seven months.
During these past three months of feeling deeply depressed and empty, have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself or that life is not worth living?

No, I haven't had any thoughts of hurting myself, and I don't feel like life isn't worth living. Even though I've been feeling incredibly empty and sad, those kinds of thoughts haven't crossed my mind.
